title: Tatamuckatakis (Great Neck Creek)
summary: Tatamuckatakis is recorded as a neck and creek in Babylon, west of Copiague Neck, now known as Great Neck and Great Neck Creek.
history_content: The place was among three meadow necks purchased from Massapeague people in 1658 and appears in Huntington records through several spellings from 1659 onward.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include tatamunehese, Yatamontitaheg, Yatamuntitahege, Tantamuntatauket, Tacamackacackee, and Tac-a-mac-a-cak-ee. The name is interpreted as meadow that trembles.

Why Place Names Matter

“In all cultures, toponyms (or placenames) are important, for they form an integral part of our history and culture.”

— Claire Bowern, Naming Bardi Places (2010), chapter opening, Aboriginal Placenames: Naming and re-naming the Australian landscape
preservation_content: Tatamuckatakis preserves the older meadow and creek name behind Great Neck Creek, where south-shore meadow purchases and later Babylon records layered multiple spellings over the same place.
